itemDispositions.reasoning: Opened `.claude/settings.json:5-88`, `scripts/ai-hooks/policy.sh:1059-1213`, and `scripts/ai-hooks/test.sh:253-301,515-522`. Claude carries 81 hand-authored native deny patterns while shared hooks separately implement the corresponding destructive Git and GitHub policies. The family-level parity smoke mitigates current drift but does not derive either representation and already needs a stash exception to preserve contextual policy behavior.

Opened `scripts/ai-hooks/edited-paths.sh:8-62`, `tidy-edited-file.sh:31-67,143-154`, `lint-coverage-check.sh:21-32`, and `stop-policy.sh:705-715`. Tidy privately repeats the shared apply-patch and file-path extraction, while three hooks carry equivalent full ESLint extension classifiers. Payload or extension changes can therefore make formatting, coverage advice, and Stop warnings observe different edited-file sets.

Opened `scripts/sensor-context-budget.ts:2-23,64-182,190-258` and its focused tests. Markdown stripping, Claude `@path` grammar, four-hop recursion, shortest-depth traversal, cycle handling, and home-relative resolution directly implement this vendor-specific sensor's documented measurement contract. A generic Markdown parser would not eliminate the vendor import semantics and would add machinery to a terminal advisory; CQ25-34 also treats the sensor as a sanctioned flat companion.

Opened `scripts/generate-baseline-conflict-recipes.ts:30-109`, its focused tests, and authored leaf 128. The extractor is formatting-sensitive but bounded to one case arm and fails loudly when the function label, arm, unquoted heredoc, or terminator shape changes. Leaf 128 explicitly retains the driver as the hand-authored recipe source and its case-arm extraction rather than making the hook-critical driver a generated splice target.

Opened `package.json:15-17`, the three workflow files, and `examples/lint-ratchet-demo/smoke.sh`. Root CI and slow drift consistently use Bun 1.3.11, matching the root package manager; only the path-scoped public demo smoke uses 1.3.14 in a fresh throwaway adopter workspace. The package's runtime contract is Bun >=1.3.0, so this provides incidental cross-patch coverage rather than demonstrated harmful inconsistency.

Opened `scripts/drift-ai/near-duplicates-runner.ts` and the near-duplicates documentation. The optional binary is installed without a version pin, its human-readable delimiters are parsed privately, and status 0 is accepted even when parsing recognizes no pairs. An upstream presentation change can therefore silently certify an empty successful result.

Opened all 249 lines of `scripts/drift-triage/triage-report-support.ts` and `scripts/drift-triage/MODULE.md`. The module deliberately owns shared parse/build helpers; concrete risks in the grouping are already covered by leaf 134, leaf 139, and CQ25-45. Splitting the remaining small location, merge, provenance, and deferral helpers would add internal files without a distinct failure or maintenance mechanism.

Opened `triage-packets.ts`, `triage-verdict-types.ts`, `triage-packet-types.ts`, and `triage-verdict-input.ts`. Packet production hand-copies verdict, severity, confidence, and required-field lists while runtime parsing enforces separate canonical arrays. The packet type widens the closed vocabularies to strings, so either copy can drift and instruct reviewers to produce records the collector rejects.

Opened `hotspots-actionability.ts`, `hotspots.ts`, their focused tests, and authored leaf 135. Baseline behavior is prominently documented in the file header and its dedicated section beginning at line 122; keeping row-actionability initialization and baseline tagging together is coherent. The demonstrated stringly lens-registration hazard in that section is already precisely covered by leaf 135.

Opened `packages/server/src/services/character-delete.ts` and its focused harness. The service first loads the character's active participant rows, then awaits another participant-list query inside a loop for every active encounter before entering the delete transaction. The test harness explicitly models that 1+N query shape, and no active-encounter-count bound exists.

Opened all of `inventory-service.ts`, its router consumer, and the services charter. Mapping, list aggregates, and create/update orchestration are sections of one cohesive inventory boundary and reuse the same mapper in request-facing operations. The documented flat-service convention favors keeping this closely related 283-line concern together; the title shows different implementation techniques but no harmful ownership split.

Opened the manual-log service, `broadcast-helpers.ts`, and `encounter-combat/MODULE.md`. Manual logs reconstruct chat options and directly invoke encounter plus chat broadcasts, while the canonical coordinator owns that ordered fan-out for other encounter-combat mutations. The module charter explicitly says request-facing entry points including `addCombatLog` own fan-out through that coordinator, so source and declared boundary disagree.

Opened the complete character-live-state plan surface, its module document, and focused tests. The sole current producer returns one character id, but the module explicitly defines multiplicity as the post-transaction contract for future compound commands, and tests pin deduplication and multi-character behavior. The generality costs only a short Set loop and creates no incorrect state or maintenance fork.

Verified the cited Tailwind sequence in 16 production sheet files and inspected representative panels. The repeated material is a fixed token sequence, while panels differ substantially in conditional rendering, headers, controls, dynamic borders, and empty states. No behavioral or visual drift was demonstrated, so a configurable wrapper would replace conventional Tailwind repetition without establishing a useful invariant.

Opened `hooks/use-surface-reset.ts:7-33`, all three callers, `stores/MODULE.md`, and CQ25-117. The options interface admits only the three named stores and requires a surface key; actual combinations correspond directly to map, combat map, and encounter tracker boundaries. The module explicitly records this hook as owner of an intentionally explicit reset set, and no invalid caller or drift is present.

Opened `use-monster-attack.ts:14-26,64-83`, the sole predicate consumer, and the drawer module maps. `StructuredMonsterAction` and its predicate define exactly which actions the mutation hook can execute; presentation consumes that public contract to decide whether to expose the matching Attack button. Moving twelve lines to a third module would not reduce coupling or prevent a demonstrated inconsistency.

Opened the shared `GridType` vocabulary and the three client declarations widening it to string. `GridBody` recognizes only square and hex, so an invalid string type-checks and silently renders no grid; the primary toolbar similarly suppresses template tools for every value except square. These direct `MapDetail.gridType` boundaries discard useful exhaustiveness.

Opened `campaign-homebrew-section.tsx:158-165` and other navigation to the same destination. The empty-state link is a literal anchor to `/homebrew`, while established callers use TanStack Router Link. This path therefore performs a document navigation and unnecessarily discards in-memory application state.

Opened the established homebrew field-error contract and representative bypassing forms. Shared fields announce and associate errors with `role=alert`, `aria-invalid`, an error id, and `aria-describedby`; eleven error-bearing homebrew field components instead render visual destructive paragraphs without control association. This is a bounded accessibility residual rather than the rejected style-only 49-site field sweep.

Opened both complete caster-selection blocks and the shared homebrew module charter. Class and subclass independently render the same caster-type and spellcasting-ability selects, including the `_none` conversion and duplicate display labels, despite already sharing options and parsing. The class-only Ritual Adept checkbox lies outside the duplicated block, and the charter admits two-consumer presentation primitives.

Opened both deletion dialogs and the existing ordinary `DeleteConfirmDialog`. Collection and entry deletion duplicate confirm-name state, trimmed matching, submit guarding, dialog/input wiring, pending cancellation, mutation-error presentation, and footer state; only entity copy and mutation side effects differ. The ordinary shared dialog does not model typed-name confirmation.

promotionCandidates.title: Fail closed when similarity-ts stdout no longer matches the supported protocol

evidence.note: The documented install command fetches the current similarity-ts release without pinning a supported version.
A zero subprocess status is accepted as success even when parsing recognizes no pairs.
The parser silently skips unrecognized stdout and has no completeness or unexpected-output signal.
Pair and score decoding depend on exact human-text markers, spacing, range punctuation, and percent formatting.

promotionCandidates.problem: The optional analyzer integrates an unpinned external binary through a private parser for human-readable stdout. A presentation change with status 0 can yield no rows and be reported as a clean successful result, creating silent false negatives.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Declare and check a supported version or use structured output if available. Treat nonempty but unrecognized successful output as a run failure and pin clean, malformed, and changed-protocol cases.
